title: Sky Gold And Diamonds Ltd - 541967 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Sky Gold guides FY27 revenue INR8,100 crore and FY30 PAT INR945 crore, targets 50%+ debt reduction in FY27 with working capital cut to 59 days.
summary.overview: Management said Q4 FY26 outpaced industry peers on wedding and festive demand, with B2B volumes steady despite the recent customs duty hike and government appeal to curb gold consumption. Net working capital days fell to 59 from 71 a year earlier, and operating cash flow improved from negative INR272 crore to negative INR45 crore for the year. Management revised its guidance framing: it will no longer give volume guidance, keeps FY30 PAT of INR945 crore, and sees 30-35% revenue CAGR with an advanced gold model that lowers reported revenue but adds margin. Phase 3 is funded wholly from internal cash, with a net debt-free balance sheet targeted by FY30.

financial_highlights.change: incl. INR3.7 crore gain on investments, INR8.4 crore exchange gain, INR4.5 crore interest income

financial_highlights.metric: Annualised Q4 revenue exit run rate

financial_highlights.change: vs 5.7% in FY25; exit run rate about 20%

segments.name: Domestic B2B (traditional and advanced gold)
segments.commentary: About 88% of revenue; no softening seen at B2B level per management. Advanced gold (job-work fee recognised as revenue) at 11.5% of FY26 business and about 20% exit rate.

segments.name: Exports / international
segments.commentary: About 12% of revenue; run rate 7-8% after Middle East disruption, with Dubai/UAE about 50% normalised. Management targets about 12% within a quarter and about 20% of sales longer term; exports are outright, not advanced gold.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance INR8,100 crore; management says this is 30-40% above initial estimates.
FY30 targets: PAT INR945 crore, sales INR18,000-19,000 crore, PAT margin 5.25% (75 bps above current), net debt nil; revenue CAGR 30-35%.
Net debt reduction of over 50% in FY27 via land sale (buyers being sought through 2-3 agencies, monetisation expected August-September 2026) and operational improvement.
Gross margin expected to expand 60-90 bps from advanced gold and studded mix; interest cost (1.25% of sales) to fall toward zero as debt is repaid.
Cash conversion target of 20-25% of PAT into operating cash flow; FY27 conversion expected to be well above this.
Receivable days expected to return to 22-23 days within 4-6 quarters.
Dividends to be funded strictly from operating cash flow; promoters move to zero salary from FY27.
capex_capacity: Capacity of 1.2 tonnes (about 1,200 kg, 14.4 tonnes per annum of gold processing); Q4 FY26 processing around 650 kg per month, about 55% utilisation.
No capacity constraint expected until March 2028; beyond that, management is considering an asset-light model via rented facilities, or a land sale followed by a buyer-built facility leased back.
Gold metal loan (GML) facility sanctioned INR170 crore; GML outstanding nil at March-end 2026, with use dependent on pricing.
Statutory auditor changed to MSKA & Associates LLP (BDO International member).
demand_pricing: B2B demand stable per management; lightweight and studded jewellery mix is the margin lever; diamond jewellery at about 1.5% of sales.
Management says 18kt is gaining share versus 22kt, which still holds 70-75% of sales; some shift toward bullion and coins noted at retail.
Advanced gold margin is 70-125 bps lower than outright gold sales, but is PAT-accretive as it avoids working capital and interest.
Management says gold price correction of about 10% in recent days is driving customer demand; gold price was about INR1,55,000 per 10g as quoted on the call.
Akshaya Tritiya on 20 April: some Q4 inventory was held back and delivered in early April, which raised inventory days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the customs duty hike and government appeal to reduce gold consumption hit revenue or volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no order softening has been seen at B2B level as the company is focused on lightweight jewellery; the retail gold exchange share reportedly rose from 20% to 40%, and it is too early to call June-July demand.

qa_highlights.question: Is the shift to lower karat and bullion/coins a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is part of the strategy; 9kt, 14kt and 18kt carry better margins, while 22kt remains 70-75% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why has gold metal loan usage dropped to zero?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GML is currently costlier than local market purchases, so it is used only when PAT-accretive; GML facility of INR170 crore remains sanctioned.

qa_highlights.question: Does the setup of a Dubai office for duty-free gold get affected by the 100 kg advanced licence restriction?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the restriction applies only to advanced authorisation licences, which the company is not using now, so there is no impact; gold availability is not seen as an issue.

qa_highlights.question: Will receivable days return to FY24 levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivable days should return to 22-23 days within 4-6 quarters as export and shorter-credit customers are prioritised.

qa_highlights.question: How does volume growth fit with 30-35% revenue CAGR, and what is the hedging policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 27-28% of growth is volume-led; the company is about 99% hedged, using MCX futures as the only tool available in India, with zero GML now.

risks_watch: Government measures on gold imports, duty changes and GML rules could hit demand or funding costs; management declined to speculate on policy.
Advanced gold mix shift makes reported revenue a weaker guide; watch volumes (kg per month), advanced gold share (exit about 20%), and the gap between gross margin and PAT.
Land sale timing (August-September 2026) and the 50%+ debt reduction in FY27 depend on execution.
Inventory days rose in Q4 FY26 due to Akshaya Tritiya timing; watch whether this reverses.
Export share needs to rise from about 12% to about 20%, while Middle East disruption has cut the run rate to 7-8%.
Management changes: Akash Talesara proposed as CEO subject to Board approval; promoter pay moves to zero salary from FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, margins and deleveraging, but guarded on demand: management repeatedly declined to give volume guidance or comment on policy, and gave inconsistent answers on advanced gold revenue and exit run rates.
key_quotes: Top line is vanity, PAT is sanity and cash in the bank is reality.
We would like to categorically state that our operations are back to back hedged.
Sky Gold maintains zero GML exposure today.
We are targeting a sustainable revenue CAGR of 30% to 35%, projecting a PAT of INR945 crores by 2030.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR8,100 crore (30-40% above initial estimates) and FY30 revenue CAGR of 30-35%, backed by a 1.2-tonne plant at about 55% utilisation with no constraint until March 2028, a gold price correction driving demand, and a 60-90 bps gross margin expansion from advanced gold and studded mix; no new capacity or firm orders are cited, so backing is only partial.
